title: Crystal Synthesizer — rich
forward_vector: I am the manifest of Crystal Synthesizer's rich face, its first round, a Study: the bundle's summer proofs, ring study and plugin face gathered beside the claims they answer, and two walks made to test the page's own words, the dispersion curve's sentence about which phonons are fast and the seven lattice hypotheses struck through the plugin's engine. I hold the fingerprint of the words each piece was laid against, and the offers the making found for the text; I never hold the entry's words.

sections.heading: The Physical Reality: Crystals as Resonators

pieces.file: Crystal Synthesizer — rich — which phonons are fast.html
pieces.title: which phonons are fast · a walk in three steps
pieces.caption: **The section's own curve, walked up to its own sentence.** First the curve ω(k) alone, with each mode's pitch to hear; then its slope, the speed a pulse's energy travels, with a row of atoms whose pulse slows to a standstill at the zone boundary; then a click sent through a chain built from that curve, beside a click through a crystal with no dispersion. The last step asks which waves arrived first. Checked headless: in this chain 250 Hz arrives at 120 ms and 7.5 kHz at 342 ms, the magnitude untouched.
pieces.near: The shape of this curve determines everything

verdicts.file: Crystal Synthesizer — rich — which phonons are fast.html
verdicts.why: A real test: the chain built from the section’s own ω(k) could have sent highs first and sends lows first (250 Hz 120 ms, 7.5 kHz 342 ms); an independent mass-spring simulation gives v_g = cos(ka/2) to four places. Walks curve, slope, click; its disagreement with the text is offer 1, stated as such.

pieces.title: the plugin's face, playable · 2026-10-24
pieces.caption: **The answer so far to the performer question.** The VST's face in the template's editor, the crystal in its screen, fed by the JavaScript port of the plugin's engine. Press *sound on*, then play keys A to K. Axis angle turns the crystal against the light and parts its two rays; Fire fans each strike from red to violet. pieces.title: the plugin's take · five minerals, 2026-10-24
pieces.caption: Thirty seconds through the plugin's C++ engine: ruby turning to its axis, diamond with Fire, zircon's split widening, labradorite low and dry, an emerald chorus. Copied from the bundle's top folder so the public face can play it.
pieces.near: How would a performer interface with this

verdicts.why: The conform error stands and the keys play without MIDI, as the caption says. But the manifest’s empty contract {} under-declares, and that is what turns conform’s soft warn into an error (conform.mjs:112-113, 497); the truthful contract {"needs":"midi"} leaves grant-missing, which is exactly Loudon’s yes in grants.json.
Tracked, 30 s stereo, copied under rich-face/ for the public face; the plugin heard beside the performer question.

offers.section: The Physical Reality: Crystals as Resonators
offers.what: "Long-wavelength phonons (small k) are slow; short-wavelength phonons are fast" has them reversed. In a chain built from the section's own ω(k), 250 Hz arrives at 120.1 ms and 7.5 kHz at 342 ms; v_g/v₀ is 1.000 at ka 0.05, 0.707 at π/2, 0.025 near π, and the phase velocity also falls (1.000 to 0.647). Suggested: long waves travel fastest, at the speed of sound, and slow to a standstill at the zone boundary; the curve's steepness at small k is the speed of sound (impedance is that times the density).

offers.section: Bravais Lattice Taxonomy: Seven into Fourteen into 230
offers.what: From reading, not from a piece: "When you add glide reflection and screw rotation, the 7 primitive systems generate 14 Bravais lattices". The 14 come from centring the 7 lattice systems (body-, face- and base-centred cells); glide and screw operations, with the 32 point groups, are what take the 14 to 230 space groups.

offers.section: Bravais Lattice Taxonomy: Seven into Fourteen into 230
offers.what: From reading: the orthorhombic entry names four Raman-active families (Ag, B₁g, B₂g, B₃g), and its hypothesis two lines on predicts "three distinct mode groups". One of the two counts wants changing.

offers.section: The Optical-Sonic Bridge: Dispersion, Anisotropy, and Resonance
offers.what: From reading, the optical half only: "the refractive index at a given frequency tells you the group velocity of light". The index gives the phase velocity, c/n; the group velocity needs its slope too, v_g = c / (n + ω dn/dω). The acoustic half stands (the slope of ω(k) is the group velocity, which the first section's walk shows), so the bridge holds as slope to slope.
